baseline.name: Allocate and copy each output operation string
baseline.approach: Generate the same Push/Pop sequence but allocate a separate string for each emitted operation.
baseline.time: O(m) for largest target m and O(m) short output strings
baseline.space: O(m) pointer output plus separately allocated operation-string payloads

archived.name: Operation pointers to shared string literals
archived.time: O(m), where m is the largest target value
archived.space: O(1) auxiliary state; O(m) returned operation-pointer allocation

why: The output sequence is identical, but constant operation labels can be shared rather than copied per output item.
quantitative_comparison: For p emitted operations, the comparator makes p string allocations in addition to its pointer-array allocation. The archive makes one pointer-array allocation and reuses two literals, eliminating those p per-string allocations/copies. No milliseconds or allocator-byte ratio is established.
tradeoffs: Consumers must free only the pointer array, never the literals or write through them. The target must be nonempty/increasing and the output allocation is unchecked.
evidence_basis: Static source inspection and stated algorithm work/storage model. Comparator is an analytical alternative, not an implemented or timed benchmark. Historical platform acceptance is separate from current local validation.
